source.author: verg
source.text: Sed si tantus amor casus cognoscere nostros et breviter Troiae supremum audire laborem, quamquam animus meminisse horret, luctuque refugit, incipiam.F
source.text_original: Sed si tantus amor casus cognoscere nostros / et breviter Troiae supremum audire laborem, / quamquam animus meminisse horret, luctuque refugit, / incipiam.F
source.text_english: But if such is your desire to learn of our fortunes and briefly to hear of Troy’s final agony, though my mind shudders to remember and recoils in grief, I shall begin.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: non calamitates miserorum, sed fragilem humanae condicionis narro statum horret animus temporum nostrorum ruinas prosequi : uiginti et eo amplius anni sunt, quod inter Constantinopolim et Alpes Iulias cotidie Romanus sanguis effunditur.
reuse.text_original: non calamitates miserorum, sed fragilem humanae condicionis narro statum — horret animus temporum nostrorum ruinas prosequi —: uiginti et eo amplius anni sunt, quod inter Constantinopolim et Alpes Iulias cotidie Romanus sanguis effunditur.
reuse.text_english: I am recounting not the misfortunes of the wretched, but the frail state of human condition; the soul shudders to follow the ruins of our times: it has been twenty and more years since, between Constantinople and the Julian Alps, Roman blood has been shed daily.
